description: Healthy intact myofibers are freshly isolated from extensor digitorum longus (EDL) muscles for use in the mechanical damage model.
goal: to obtain myofibers for mechanical damage and subsequent co-culture experiments
span_chunk: To obtain mechanically damaged myofibers, healthy intact myofibers freshly isolated from extensor digitorum longus (EDL) muscles were mechanically damaged with a Pasteur pipette in a culture dish

description: Using a Pasteur pipette, the isolated healthy intact myofibers are mechanically damaged in a culture dish to create damaged myofibers (DMDFs).
goal: to produce damaged myofibers for studying their effect on satellite cell activation
span_chunk: healthy intact myofibers freshly isolated from extensor digitorum longus (EDL) muscles were mechanically damaged with a Pasteur pipette in a culture dish

description: The damage to the myofibers is confirmed based on their shrunken morphology.
goal: to ensure successful mechanical damage of myofibers
span_chunk: the damage was confirmed based on shrunken morphology

description: Intact myofibers are co-cultured with damaged myofibers to examine the direct stimulation of satellite cell activation and proliferation.
goal: to assess the effect of damaged myofibers on the activation and proliferation of satellite cells
span_chunk: This co-culture of intact myofibers with damaged myofibers allowed us to examine whether DMDFs directly stimulate the activation and proliferation of satellite cells associated with the healthy intact myofibers.

description: Immunofluorescence analysis is conducted to detect the presence of MYOD+ and Ki67+ satellite cells on intact myofibers when co-cultured with damaged myofibers.
goal: to visualize and quantify the activation and cell cycle entry of satellite cells
span_chunk: Immunofluorescence analysis revealed the presence of a higher proportion of MYOD+ satellite cells on intact myofibers when they were co-cultured with damaged myofibers

task_name: Wash out damaged myofibers and culture media
description: After co-culturing, the damaged myofibers and the culture media containing DMDFs are washed out and replaced with fresh DMEM for an additional culture period.
goal: to investigate if satellite cells can revert to a quiescent state after removal of DMDFs
span_chunk: The damaged myofibers and the culture media containing DMDFs were then washed out and replaced with fresh DMEM and cultured for an additional 24 h

description: The transverse diameter of satellite cells associated with intact myofibers is measured after co-culture with damaged myofibers and after washing out the damaged myofibers and culture media.
goal: to evaluate the morphological changes of satellite cells in response to DMDFs
span_chunk: The transverse diameter of satellite cells associated with intact myofibers was evidently increased upon co-culture with damaged myofibers and became smaller when the damaged myofibers and culture media were washed out

description: LUHMES cells are differentiated into post-mitotic neurons by replacing the proliferation medium with differentiation medium and culturing for a total of 5 days.
goal: to obtain fully differentiated post-mitotic neurons for the assay
span_chunk: LUHMES were grown on cell culture flasks in proliferation medium... When cells were 50–60% confluent they were differentiated by replacing media with differentiation media... After two days, LUHMES were trypsinized and replated onto the appropriate plates for a further 3 days before becoming fully differentiated.

task_name: Transduce LUHMES with GFP-expressing lentiviral particles
description: Low passage proliferating LUHMES are transduced with LV-GFP for 24 hours, followed by a media change and additional 72-hour culture before experiments.
goal: to generate GFP LUHMES for visualization in the assay
span_chunk: GFP LUHMES were generated by transducing non-differentiated LUHMES with GFP-expressing lentiviral particles (LV-GFP)... Low passage (p3-p5) proliferating LUHMES, seeded at 1.5x10 6 cells per T75 flask, were transduced with LV-GFP for 24 hours.

task_name: Co-culture GFP LUHMES with treated astrocytes
description: GFP LUHMES are replated onto astrocytes treated with MAB391 or MAB002, and co-cultures are maintained in differentiation media for 72 hours.
goal: to assess the support of astrocytes for neurons under the influence of IGF1R reduction
span_chunk: On day 3 GFP LUHMES were replated onto treated astrocytes, and at this point the monoclonal antibody was removed. Co-cultures were then maintained in differentiation media for 72 hours.

description: After 72 hours of co-culture, treat the co-cultures with 50 μM H2O2 for 2 hours.
goal: to induce stress and assess astrocytic protection against external stress
span_chunk: After which co-cultures were treated with 50 μM H2O2 for 2 hours.

task_name: Fix and stain co-cultures for neurite outgrowth assay
description: Co-cultures are fixed with paraformaldehyde, permeabilized, blocked, and stained with Hoechst 33342 for nuclei visualization.
goal: to prepare co-cultures for neurite length measurement
span_chunk: GFP LUHMES were co-cultured with astrocytes for 72 hours as described above, before fixation with 4% (w/v) paraformaldehyde.

task_name: Capture images and measure neurite length
description: Images of the co-cultures are captured and neurite length is measured using the Simple Neurite Tracer plugin in ImageJ.
goal: to quantify neurite outgrowth and assess the effect of astrocyte support
span_chunk: Five images were captured of each coverslip... Neurite length was measured using an ImageJ plugin called Simple Neurite Tracer.

description: Cut formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) lung tissues into 4-µm-thick sections for immunofluorescence staining.
goal: to obtain thin sections of lung tissue for subsequent staining and analysis
span_chunk: lung tissues were FFPE, and lung sections were cut (4-µm-thick sections) for immunofluorescence staining.

description: Boil the lung tissue sections in sodium carbonate buffer and permeabilize in PBS with Triton X-100.
goal: to remove paraffin and rehydrate the tissue sections for antigen retrieval
span_chunk: After deparaffinization and rehydration, tissue sections were boiled for 20 min in 10-mM sodium carbonate buffer for antigen retrieval.

description: Incubate lung sections with a blocking buffer containing BSA and donkey serum to prevent non-specific antibody binding.
goal: to reduce background staining by blocking non-specific binding sites
span_chunk: Samples were incubated with a blocking buffer (PBS with 2% BSA and 2% of donkey serum; Sigma-Aldrich) for 1 h at room temperature.

description: Stain the lung sections with primary antibodies against citrullinated histone H3 and myeloperoxidase (MPO) in blocking buffer.
goal: to label neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) components in the lung tissue
span_chunk: stained in blocking buffer with rabbit anti-human antibodies directed against citrullinated histone H3 (Abcam, Ab5103; 1:100 in blocking buffer) and with goat anti-human antibodies directed against MPO (R&D Systems, AF3667; 1:40 in blocking buffer) for 1 h at room temperature.

description: Incubate lung sections with secondary antibodies conjugated with fluorophores and DAPI for nuclear staining.
goal: to visualize the primary antibodies and cell nuclei under fluorescence microscopy
span_chunk: secondary donkey anti-rabbit IgG antibodies conjugated with Alexa Fluor 568 (1:200 in blocking buffer) and donkey anti-goat IgG antibodies conjugated with Alexa Fluor 488 (1:200 in blocking buffer) were added in blocking buffer containing DAPI (1:1,000) and incubated for 2 h in the dark at room temperature.

description: Mount the stained lung sections with ProLong Antifade reagent and store them at room temperature in the dark overnight.
goal: to preserve the fluorescence signal for microscopy analysis
span_chunk: Finally, samples were mounted with 10 µl of ProLong Antifade reagent (Thermo Fisher Scientific) on glass slides and stored at room temperature in the dark overnight.

description: Analyze all samples by fluorescence microscopy using standard filter sets to capture images of the stained lung sections.
goal: to visualize and capture the distribution of NETs in the lung tissue
span_chunk: All samples were analyzed by fluorescence microscopy using standard filter sets.

task_name: Quantify NET volume using confocal microscopy and software analysis
description: Acquire Z-stack pictures with confocal microscopy and use Imaris software for three-dimensional reconstruction and quantification of NET volume.
goal: to measure the volume of NETs present in the lung tissue
span_chunk: To quantify the volume of NETs present in the lung tissue, six fields (magnification, 20×) were analyzed per patients, Z-stack pictures were acquired, and Imaris software was used.

task_name: Screen entire lung sections for NET-infiltrating areas
description: Scan entire lung sections with the Nanozoomer system and manually screen for areas rich in structures staining double positive for Cit-H3 and MPO.
goal: to assess the presence of NETs in entire lung sections
span_chunk: To assess for the presence of NETs in entire lung sections, sections were entirely scanned using the Nanozoomer 2.0-HT system.

description: Create pCRISPR-SacB-gDNA plasmids encoding the RNA guides necessary to drive the Cas9-dependent double-stranded break to the desired site within the bacterial genome.
goal: to enable targeted gene knockout using CRISPR/Cas9
span_chunk: The pCRISPR-SacB-gDNA plasmid carries the synthetic DNA fragment (gDNA), transcribed from a constitutive promoter, encoding the RNA guide necessary to drive the Cas9-dependent double stranded break to the desired site within the bacterial genome.

task_name: Transform E. coli with pCRISPR-SacB-gDNA plasmids
description: Introduce the pCRISPR-SacB-gDNA plasmids into E. coli BL21(DE3)Δ ompA (pCasRed) strain to facilitate CRISPR/Cas9-mediated gene editing.
goal: to initiate the CRISPR/Cas9 gene knockout process
span_chunk: E. coli BL21(DE3)Δ ompA was used since we observed that the strain maintained good transformation efficiencies even in the presence of pCasRed plasmid.

task_name: Select colonies on LB plates with antibiotics
description: Grow transformed E. coli on LB plates supplemented with chloramphenicol and kanamycin to select for colonies that have successfully incorporated the pCRISPR-SacB-gDNA plasmids.
goal: to isolate E. coli colonies that carry the CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing components
span_chunk: Colonies were selected on LB plates supplemented with Cm and Km.

description: Create synthetic oligonucleotides (donor DNA, dDNA) with homology arms for targeted gene deletions or mutations.
goal: to provide templates for homology-directed repair after CRISPR/Cas9-mediated cleavage
span_chunk: Donor DNAs were designed with homology arms of equal length upstream and downstream from the deletion.

task_name: Co-transform E. coli with pCRISPR-SacB-gDNA and dDNA
description: Introduce both the pCRISPR-SacB-gDNA plasmid and the corresponding donor DNA into E. coli to facilitate gene knockout and repair.
goal: to achieve targeted gene deletions or mutations in E. coli
span_chunk: Each pCRISPR-SacB-gDNA plasmid, with its corresponding dDNA, was used to transform E. coli BL21(DE3)Δ ompA (pCasRed) strain.

task_name: Analyze colonies by PCR for gene deletions
description: Perform PCR on selected colonies to identify those carrying the desired gene deletions or mutations.
goal: to confirm successful gene editing
span_chunk: From each transformation ten colonies were randomly selected and analyzed by PCR to identify those carrying the 30 bp deletion and to establish the 'success rate' of mutagenesis.

description: Grow mutant E. coli colonies in LB supplemented with sucrose to eliminate the pCRISPR-SacB-gDNA plasmid, exploiting the toxicity of the sacB gene in the presence of sucrose.
goal: to remove the pCRISPR-SacB-gDNA plasmid after gene mutation
span_chunk: E. coli strains carrying any pCRISPR-SacB plasmid derivative can survive in the presence of sucrose only if they rapidly lose the plasmid.

task_name: Prepare competent cells from cured cultures
description: Prepare competent cells from the overnight cultures of E. coli that have been cured of the pCRISPR-SacB-gDNA plasmid.
goal: to enable subsequent rounds of transformation for multi-gene knockouts
span_chunk: Once a mutant colony is selected by colony PCR, it can be inoculated in sucrose-containing LB and the overnight culture can be directly used to make competent cells for the subsequent mutagenesis step.

description: Assemble the complex of CRISPR RNA (crRNA) targeting the Pax5 promoter and trans-activating crRNA (tracrRNA) to be used as Pax5 gRNA for in vitro enChIP.
goal: to create a specific guide RNA complex for targeting the Pax5 promoter
span_chunk: The complex of CRISPR RNA (crRNA) targeting the Pax5 promoter and trans-activating crRNA (tracrRNA) was used as Pax5 gRNA for in vitro enChIP.

description: Fragment the chromatin DNA to an average length of about 2 kbp to facilitate the isolation of the target region.
goal: to produce DNA fragments suitable for target region isolation
span_chunk: Briefly, after fragmentation of chromatin DNA (the average length of fragments was about 2 kbp), the target region was isolated by iChIP or in vitro enChIP.

description: Use in vitro enChIP to isolate the target region from the fragmented chromatin DNA.
goal: to capture the specific genomic region of interest
span_chunk: the target region was isolated by iChIP or in vitro enChIP.

description: Purify the DNA after the target region has been isolated to remove any contaminants and non-specifically bound DNA.
goal: to obtain clean DNA for library preparation
span_chunk: After purification of DNA, DNA libraries were prepared using TruSeq ChIP Sample Prep Kit (Illumina)

description: Prepare DNA libraries using the TruSeq ChIP Sample Prep Kit, selectively concentrating DNA fragments around 0.4 kbp in length.
goal: to create DNA libraries suitable for next-generation sequencing
span_chunk: DNA libraries were prepared using TruSeq ChIP Sample Prep Kit (Illumina); in this preparation step, DNA fragments around 0.4 kbp in length were selectively concentrated.

description: Subject the prepared DNA libraries to DNA sequencing using the HiSeq platform according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
goal: to sequence the DNA libraries and generate data for analysis
span_chunk: The libraries were subjected to DNA sequencing using the HiSeq platform according to the manufacturer’s protocol.

description: Map NGS data onto the reference genome galGal4 using ELAND and detect narrow peaks using Model-based Analysis of ChIP-Seq 2 (MACS2) with default parameters.
goal: to identify genomic regions that interact with the Pax5 promoter
span_chunk: NGS data were mapped onto the reference genome galGal4 using ELAND. Narrow peaks of each iChIP-Seq dataset were detected using Model-based Analysis of ChIP-Seq 2 (MACS2) with default parameters.

description: Generate images of NGS peaks using Integrative Genomics Viewer (IGV) to visualize the genomic interactions.
goal: to visually represent the identified genomic interactions
span_chunk: Images of NGS peaks were generated using Integrative Genomics Veiwer (IGV).

description: Position worms for live imaging and microirradiation using slides with agarose pads or live imaging petri dishes, place worms in M9 with polystyrene beads, and cover with a coverslip or agarose pad.
goal: to set up the live imaging environment for microirradiation
span_chunk: Worms were positioned for live imaging and microirradiation using both 1’x3’x.04’ slides with the worms on top of a 3% agarose pad made with M9, or using a live imaging petri dish...

description: Locate nuclei in the germline, focus on the center of target nuclei, and microirradiate using a pulsed laser at specified intensity for each nucleus.
goal: to induce precise double-strand breaks in the DNA of targeted nuclei
span_chunk: Nuclei in the appropriate region of the germline were located and the Z-plane was focused on the center of the target nuclei before microirradiation. Target nuclei were selected at the center of each nucleus and microirradiated using a single pulse with Andor micropoint 365nm pulsed laser...

description: Acquire images at 2-minute intervals, centering on the z-plane coordinate of microirradiation, and adjust the position of the center Z stack as needed to keep nuclei in focus.
goal: to capture the response of nuclei to microirradiation over time
span_chunk: Time series projects of microirradiated live worms were created using Metamorph Multidimensional Acquisition. Images were aquired at 2 min periods, imaging a 9 μm range centered on the z-plane coordinate of microirradiation at 1 μm intervals resulting in 10 image stacks per time point.

task_name: Process and analyze live imaging data
description: Process imaged stacks to create a maximum projection for each time point and score nuclei for foci in FIJI-Image J, recording the size and number of foci.
goal: to analyze the formation and characteristics of foci in microirradiated nuclei
span_chunk: Imaged stacks from live imaging were processed in MetaMorph to create a maximum projection for each time point. Nuclei were scored for foci in FIJI-Image J. Foci were counted in microirradiated nuclei and all nuclei immediately adjacent were scored as negative controls.

description: Submerge the entire slide in M9 to gently remove the coverslip, then transfer the worms to a petri dish for recovery with a glass pipet.
goal: to safely recover the microirradiated worms for further analysis
span_chunk: To recover worms after microirradiation, the entire slide was submerged in M9 and the coverslip gently pried off, then M9 was emptied into a petri dish and worms were recovered with a glass pipet.

description: Dissect worms to extract their gonads, fix and stain with appropriate antibodies and DAPI, and image using a fluorescence microscope.
goal: to visualize and analyze the DNA damage response at the site of microirradiation
span_chunk: Worms were dissected to extract their gonads which were fixed and stained as in (38) and are as follows: RAD-51 (Rabbit to RAD-51 1:10, 000; ModEncod), GFP (Chicken to GFP 1:500; Abcam), HIM-8 (Rabbit to HIM-8 1:1, 000 Novus) SYP-1 (Goat to SYP-1 1:500).

description: Cortical and hippocampal neuron cultures are prepared from mouse embryos, collected in Dissection media, and cultivated in Neuronal complete medium.
goal: to establish primary neuron cultures for cryopreservation
span_chunk: Cortical and hippocampal neuron cultures were prepared from mouse embryos (E15.5; strain C57BL/6J). Tissue specimen was collected in Dissection media and culture cultivated in Neuronal complete medium.

description: High-density neuronal cultures are plated on coverslips and grown in tissue culture plates.
goal: to grow neurons for subsequent cryopreservation
span_chunk: High-density (750–1000 cells/mm2) neuronal cultures were plated and grown on 12 mm diameter coverslips put into 24-well plastic tissue culture plates.

description: Primary neuronal cultures are transduced with GFP-expressing pLVTH virus at DIV4 using a specific multiplicity of infection.
goal: to introduce genetic material into neurons before cryopreservation
span_chunk: Primary neuronal cultures were transduced at days in vitro 4 (DIV4) with viruses at a multiplicity of infection (MOI) 2.

description: Neurons are treated with FGFb and EGF for 10 minutes.
goal: to stimulate neuronal growth and health prior to cryopreservation
span_chunk: Neurons were treated with 10 ng/ml FGFb, 5 ng/ml EGF for 10 min.

task_name: Amplify Targeted TF or CoREG ORFs
description: Amplify targeted transcription factor (TF) or co-regulator (CoREG) open reading frames (ORFs) using high-fidelity Phusion polymerase with GC buffer supplemented with 10% glycerol, and optimize the PCR conditions if necessary.
goal: to obtain amplified ORFs for cloning into vectors
span_chunk: Targeted TF or CoREG ORFs were typically amplified using high-fidelity Phusion polymerase (New England Biolabs, https://www.neb.com/ ) using the manufacturer's GC buffer supplemented with 10% glycerol.

description: Design primers to produce a fragment without a stop codon and with a 5′-CACC nucleotide tailing added to the forward primer for directional cloning into the pENTR vectors.
goal: to prepare DNA fragments for directional cloning
span_chunk: Primers were designed to produce a fragment without a stop codon, and with a 5′-CACC nucleotide tailing added to the forward primer as required for directional cloning into the pENTR vectors.

description: Screen kanamycin-resistant colonies for inserts of the correct size and orientation by colony PCR or by restriction digestion of candidate plasmids.
goal: to verify the presence and correct orientation of inserts in the vector
span_chunk: Kanamycin-resistant colonies were then screened for inserts of the correct size and orientation by colony PCR or by restriction digestion of candidate plasmids.

description: Confirm the sequence of cloned inserts by single-read paired-end Sanger dideoxy sequencing, and design internal primers for clones longer than 1200 bp to complete the sequence confirmation.
goal: to validate the sequence of the cloned ORFs
span_chunk: The sequence of cloned inserts was confirmed by single-read paired-end Sanger dideoxy sequencing. For clones longer than 1200 bp, internal primers were designed to complete the sequence confirmation.

description: Mice are brought into the dimly lit testing room to habituate for a minimum of 30 minutes prior to each training session.
goal: to reduce stress and familiarize mice with the testing environment
span_chunk: Mice were brought into the dimly lit (10% fluorescent lighting) testing room to habituate for a minimum of 30 min prior to each training session as testing was conducted with the house light off.

description: Mice are trained on the Habituation stage, Initial Touch, Must Touch Stimuli, Must Initiate, and Punish Incorrect stages to learn to interact with the touchscreen and receive rewards.
goal: to teach mice to use the touchscreen and prepare them for the visual discrimination task
span_chunk: First, mice were trained on the Habituation stage, which involved learning to collect a reward when the tray illuminated, and they were required to complete 50 trials within 20 min on two consecutive sessions. Then they moved to Initial Touch, where they learnt to touch the stimuli (white square) on the screen to receive a 3× reward or after 30 s of no activity they received a single reward. Mice were progressed to Must Touch Stimuli after completing 100 trials within 30 min or after a maximum of five sessions on Initial Touch. Mice were now required to touch the stimuli to receive a reward and again complete 100 trials in under 30 min. Following this step, mice moved to Must Initiate where they were required to enter the reward tray to start the trial and they were now required to complete 100 trials in 60 min. Then finally mice moved to Punish Incorrect where a time-out occurred if they touched the incorrect location and they were required to complete 100 trials in under 60 min with at least 70% correct.

description: Mice are required to discriminate between two visual stimuli and learn which stimulus is associated with a reward, completing 100 trials in under 60 minutes with at least 80% correct.
goal: to assess the ability of mice to learn and discriminate between two different visual stimuli
span_chunk: The VD task required rodents to discriminate between two visual stimuli and to learn which stimulus was associated with a reward. Within each trial, two stimuli were presented and if the correct one was selected the mouse received a reward. Mice were required to complete 100 trials in under 60 min and achieve at least 80% correct.

description: If mice choose the wrong window during the VD task, the image is repeated in that same window until the correct image is selected.
goal: to prevent the development of a side bias and ensure learning of the correct stimulus
span_chunk: Correction trials are critical to this protocol to prevent mice simply selecting one window, which would be rewarded on 50% of trials. If they chose the wrong window, the image would be repeated in that same window until the mouse selected the correct image.

description: After acquiring the VD task, the contingency is switched so the previously unrewarded stimulus must now be selected and the previously rewarded stimulus is now incorrect, testing until reaching 80% correct or a maximum of 20 sessions.
goal: to measure behavioral flexibility by assessing the rate of acquisition of the new pairing
span_chunk: Once this task was acquired, the contingency was switched for reversal so the previously unrewarded stimulus must now be selected and the previously rewarded stimulus is now incorrect. The rate of acquisition of the new pairing provides a measure of behavioral flexibility and testing was conducted until reaching the criteria of 80% correct or a maximum of 20 sessions.

task_name: In vitro generation of CD8+ CD28- T cells
description: Enriched A-CD8+ T cells are stimulated with B-APCs in the presence of IL-2, IL-7, and IL-15 in 24-well plates for 9 days to expand CD8+ CD28- T cells.
goal: to expand CD8+ CD28- T cells with suppressive capacity
span_chunk: Enriched A-CD8+ T cells (2×10^6 cells) were stimulated with B-APCs (1×10^6 cells) in 24-well plates in the presence of IL-2(20 U/ml), IL-7 (50 ng/ml) and IL-15 (50 ng/ml). After 9 days’ incubation, in vitro-expanded CD8+ CD28- T cells were enriched.

task_name: CFSE labeling of A-CD4+ T cells
description: A-CD4+ T cells are labeled with CFSE to track their proliferation when cocultured with APCs and CD8+ CD28- T cells.
goal: to assess the proliferation of CD4+ T cells
span_chunk: Then, CFSE-labeled A-CD4+ T cells (CD4+ T cells from individual A) (5×10^4/well) were cocultured with B-APCs (5×10^4/well) or I-APCs (5×10^4/well) in the presence or absence of in vitro-expanded CD8+ CD28- T cells (2.5×10^4/well) in 96-well round bottom plate for 7 days and 11 days.

description: CFSE-labeled A-CD4+ T cells are cocultured with B-APCs or I-APCs and in vitro-expanded CD8+ CD28- T cells in a 96-well plate to assess the suppressive activity of CD8+ CD28- T cells.
goal: to evaluate the suppressive capacity of CD8+ CD28- T cells in vitro
span_chunk: CFSE-labeled A-CD4+ T cells (5×10^4/well) were cocultured with B-APCs (5×10^4/well) or I-APCs (5×10^4/well) in the presence or absence of in vitro-expanded CD8+ CD28- T cells (2.5×10^4/well) in 96-well round bottom plate for 7 days and 11 days.

task_name: Assessment of CD4+ T cell proliferation
description: The proliferation of CD4+ T cells is measured using the CFSE dilution assay after coculture with CD8+ CD28- T cells and APCs.
goal: to determine the effect of CD8+ CD28- T cells on CD4+ T cell proliferation
span_chunk: CFSE diluted assay was used to assess the proliferation of CD4+ T cells.

description: Cells are treated with formaldehyde to cross-link proteins to DNA, which preserves protein-DNA interactions for subsequent immunoprecipitation.
goal: to preserve protein-DNA interactions
span_chunk: approximately 20 million cells were cross-linked with 1% formaldehyde for 10 min at room temperature

description: Cells are lysed and nuclei are collected to isolate chromatin for immunoprecipitation.
goal: to isolate chromatin from cells
span_chunk: Cells were washed with cold PBS...resuspended in 1 ml cell lysis buffer...incubated on ice for 10 min followed by centrifugation at 2,500 rpm for 5 min at 4°C to collect the nuclei.

description: Nuclei are lysed and chromatin is sheared to an average length of 700 bp by sonication.
goal: to shear chromatin for immunoprecipitation
span_chunk: Nuclei were resuspended in nuclear lysis buffer...Chromatin was sonicated to an average length of 700 bp followed by removing the cell debris by centrifugation.

description: Antibodies specific to symmetrically methylated H4R3 are used to precipitate the chromatin fragments of interest.
goal: to enrich for chromatin fragments with symmetrically methylated H4R3
span_chunk: The supernatant containing sonicated chromatin was diluted with ChIP buffer...Samples were precleared...The supernatant was collected...and the remaining 90% was used for capturing chromatin by rotating the complexes overnight at 4°C using indicated antibodies.

description: The antibody-chromatin complexes are washed to remove non-specifically bound DNA and then eluted.
goal: to purify the antibody-bound chromatin
span_chunk: Beads were then washed sequentially three times with a low-salt buffer...Chromatin was eluted in an elution buffer.

description: Cross-links are reversed by heating and the DNA is purified from the protein-DNA complexes.
goal: to retrieve purified DNA for sequencing
span_chunk: Chromatin was eluted...and reverse cross-linked by adding 0.3 M NaCl at 65°C overnight. Eluted DNA was precipitated, treated with proteinase K at 45°C for 2h and purified with Qiagen Min-Elute PCR purification columns.

description: Purified DNA is used to prepare sequencing libraries compatible with the Illumina platform.
goal: to prepare DNA libraries for sequencing
span_chunk: DNA extracted from the chromatin bound to respective targets and their appropriate controls was used for preparing the DNA sequencing libraries using NEXTflex TM Illumina ChIP-Seq Library Preparation Kit.

description: Sequencing of the prepared libraries is performed on an Illumina NextSeq500 platform.
goal: to sequence the enriched DNA fragments
span_chunk: Sequencing of these libraries was done on Illumina NextSeq500.

description: Sequenced reads are mapped to the KSHV genome and analyzed for enriched peaks corresponding to symmetrically methylated H4R3.
goal: to identify genomic regions enriched for symmetrically methylated H4R3
span_chunk: the sequences obtained from input, control IgG antibody and specific antibody samples were mapped to the KSHV genome...Mapped reads were analyzed for enriched peaks in ChIP samples.

description: Dilute selected siRNA SMARTpools to 0.3 µM in 1× siRNA buffer and dispense into black 384-well plates.
goal: to prepare siRNA SMARTpools for transfection
span_chunk: Selected siRNA SMARTpools were diluted to 0.3 µM in 1× siRNA buffer and dispensed in black 384-well plates (Corning).

description: Add Dharmafect 1 diluted in HBSS to the siRNA SMARTpools, incubate to allow complex formation, and seed MeWo cells onto the complexes.
goal: to transfect MeWo cells with siRNA complexes
span_chunk: To this, 10 µl Dharmafect 1 diluted in HBSS to a final concentration of 0.07% was added using the Multidrop 384. Following a 20 min incubation to enable complex formation, 2.5×10 3 MeWo cells in 40 µl media were seeded on to the complexes bringing the final volume of transfection to 60 µl in each well.

description: Incubate the transfected MeWo cells for 48 hours at 37°C in a humidified incubator with 5% CO2.
goal: to allow for siRNA uptake and gene silencing
span_chunk: Plates were incubated for 48 h at 37°C in a humidified incubator with 5% CO2 before infection.

description: Remove media from the plates, add VZV-eGFP-infected MeWo cells diluted in growth media, and incubate.
goal: to infect MeWo cells with VZV-eGFP for replication assays
span_chunk: To infect, media was removed from plates by inversion and ∼25 colony forming units of VZV-eGFP-infected MeWo cells (vaccine strain Oka) were seeded on to the complexes using the Multidrop 384.

description: Measure virus growth as a function of eGFP fluorescence from 44 to 72 hours post-infection in 3-hour intervals.
goal: to assess VZV replication in transfected cells
span_chunk: Virus growth was measured in 3 h intervals as a function of eGFP fluorescence from 44 to 72 h post-infection.

task_name: Calculate and normalize VZV replication slopes
description: Calculate virus replication slopes over the linear phase and normalize to mock transfected wells on individual assay plates.
goal: to quantify VZV replication efficiency
span_chunk: Virus replication slopes over the linear phase were calculated and normalized to mock transfected wells on individual assay plates, and the mean replication slope from six replicates used for subsequent data analyses.

task_name: Express MIG reporter in BL21(DE3) cells
description: Grow overnight cultures of BL21(DE3) cells expressing MIG reporter in LB, subculture, induce with IPTG, and allow protein expression to proceed.
goal: to produce the MIG reporter protein for subsequent analysis
span_chunk: MIG was expressed using BL21(DE3). For overexpression assays, overnight cultures grown in LB were subcultured 1:100 in fresh LB, grown to an OD 600 of ∼0.5 at 37°C, moved to 30°C, and induced with 0.5 mM isopropyl β- d -1-thiogalactopyranoside (Gold Bio), and protein expression was allowed to proceed for 1 h.

task_name: Lyse cells and prepare soluble lysate
description: Resuspend cell pellets in MIG buffer, lyse cells using a tip sonicator, and centrifuge to obtain the soluble lysate.
goal: to obtain a clear lysate containing the MIG reporter protein for splicing assay
span_chunk: Cell pellets were resuspended in MIG buffer (50 mM Tris [pH 8.0], 20 mM NaCl, 10% glycerol) and lysed on ice using a tip sonicator. Samples were pelleted at 20,000 × g, and soluble lysate was assayed.

description: Take a time zero sample and store at –20°C, then incubate the sample lysate with zinc acetate at indicated concentrations for 16 h or 24 h depending on the DnaB variant.
goal: to assess the effect of zinc on the splicing of the MIG reporter
span_chunk: A time zero sample was taken and stored at –20°C, while the sample lysate was incubated at 16°C for ∼16 h for M. smegmatis DnaBi1 and ∼24 h for M. leprae DnaB. Zinc acetate was added at the indicated concentrations immediately prior to incubation.

description: After 1-h incubation with zinc, treat samples with a 2× excess of EDTA and incubate further as indicated.
goal: to verify that the inhibition of splicing by zinc is reversible
span_chunk: To verify that zinc-mediated splicing inhibition was reversible, following 1-h incubation with zinc, samples were treated with a 2× excess of EDTA and incubated further as indicated.

description: Mix samples with Laemmli sample buffer containing β-mercaptoethanol and separate on Tris-glycine gels.
goal: to resolve the protein products for in-gel fluorescence detection
span_chunk: Samples were separated on 8% to 16% Tris-glycine gels (Bio-Rad) using Laemmli sample buffer (Bio-Rad) containing 1% β-mercaptoethanol.

description: Use an Amersham model 680 imager to detect GFP fluorescence in the gel.
goal: to visualize and analyze the splicing of the MIG reporter
span_chunk: GFP-containing products were detected with an Amersham model 680 imager (GE Healthcare).

description: Analyze the gel images using ImageJ software for quantitation of the GFP signal.
goal: to quantify the splicing efficiency of the MIG reporter
span_chunk: ImageJ was used for quantitation, and GraphPad Prism (v7.02) was used for analysis.

description: Design variable length probes based on gene models, full-length cDNA, and RNA-Seq contigs. Repeat-mask and eliminate non-specific probes to create a unique probe set.
goal: to generate a specific probe set for sequence capture
span_chunk: Variable length probes (50- to 100-mers) were generated at a 5-bp step across the entire sequence space. Individual probes were repeat-masked by removing probes that had an average 15-mer frequency >200... Probe sequences with more than 25 matches in the target set were eliminated from consideration.

description: Fragment genomic DNA and prepare Illumina TruSeq Paired End libraries. Perform size fractionation if necessary and purify the libraries.
goal: to create a library of DNA fragments suitable for sequence capture
span_chunk: 1 μg genomic DNA was fragmented into a 200–300 bp size range... Libraries were utilized either with or without size fractionation... The TruSeq DNA libraries were purified using AmPure XP Beads.

description: Enrich for correctly ligated DNA fragments using ligation-mediated PCR (LM-PCR) and purify the amplified sample library.
goal: to amplify DNA fragments that are correctly ligated with adapters
span_chunk: To enrich for correctly ligated DNA fragments, 20 μl of the TruSeq DNA library were used as template in the pre-capture LM-PCR reaction... LM-PCR cycling, clean-up and elution of the sample were as described previously.

description: Add Plant Capture Enhancer to the amplified sample library, dry the mixture, and hybridize with the Exome Library in a thermocycler.
goal: to hybridize the DNA library with the designed probes for sequence capture
span_chunk: Prior to hybridization 10 μl of Roche NimbleGen's proprietary Plant Capture Enhancer were added to a 1.5-ml tube containing 1 μg of the amplified sample library... The hybridization sample (15 μl) was incubated in a thermocycler at 47°C for 64–72 h.

task_name: Perform Affinity Purification of Captured DNA
description: Use Streptavidin Dynabeads to bind the biotinylated probes and captured DNA, and wash with various buffers to remove non-specifically bound DNA.
goal: to purify the DNA that has been specifically captured by the probes
span_chunk: The hybridization sample was added to the wet Dynabeads and mixed thoroughly by pipetting up and down... Dynabeads plus bound DNA were washed by adding 100 μl SC Wash Buffer I and vortexing for 10 sec.

description: Amplify the bead-bound captured library using LM-PCR and purify the amplified DNA.
goal: to amplify the DNA that has been captured and bound to the probes
span_chunk: The bead-bound captured library was amplified using LM-PCR... Both LM-PCR reactions were combined and cleaned-up using the Qiaquick PCR purification kit.

description: Quantify the DNA using a Qubit fluorometer and analyze the size distribution with an Agilent Bioanalyzer.
goal: to assess the quantity and quality of the amplified captured DNA library
span_chunk: The DNA was quantified using a Qubit 2.0 fluorometer... Libraries were analyzed electrophoretically using the Agilent 2100 Bioanalyzer.

description: Replace the fliG gene on the chromosome with a pHluorin(M153R)-fliG allele using the λ Red homologous recombination system.
goal: to create Salmonella strains with a pH-sensitive GFP derivative for pH imaging
span_chunk: The fliG gene on the chromosome is replaced by a pHluorin(M153R)-fliG allele using the λ Red homologous recombination system.

description: Purify pHluorin(M153R) from BL21(DE3)pLysS carrying pYVM007 and pHluorin(M153R)-FliG-His from BL21(DE3)pLysS carrying pYVM013 using Ni-NTA affinity chromatography.
goal: to obtain pure pH-sensitive GFP derivatives for calibration and imaging
span_chunk: pHluorin(M153R) was purified from the soluble fractions of BL21(DE3)pLysS carrying pYVM007... pHluorin(M153R)-FliG-His was purified by nickel-nitrilotriacetic acid (Ni-NTA) affinity chromatography from the soluble fractions of BL21(DE3)pLysS carrying pYVM013.

task_name: Set up high-resolution pH imaging system
description: Build an optical system on an inverted fluorescence microscope with specific lenses, filters, and camera, and control the system with MetaMorph software.
goal: to establish the imaging setup for detecting local pH differences within living cells
span_chunk: An optical system was built on an inverted fluorescence microscope... The high-speed wavelength switcher and the EMCCD camera were controlled by MetaMorph 3.6 software.

task_name: Capture fluorescence images of Salmonella cells
description: Observe Salmonella cells expressing pHluorin(M153R) derivatives under the microscope and capture images with a xenon lamp through excitation filters, using a high-speed wavelength switcher.
goal: to obtain fluorescence images for pH measurement
span_chunk: Salmonella cells expressing pHluorin(M153R), pHluorin(M153R)-FliG... were observed under a custom-built microscope... The pHluorin(M153R) probe was excited by a xenon lamp with two excitation filters.

task_name: Analyze fluorescence images for pH determination
description: Determine the cytoplasmic pH by analyzing the ratio of fluorescence intensity in the 410-nm and 470-nm excitation wavelength images, and subtract the background intensity.
goal: to calculate the cytoplasmic pH of each cell based on fluorescence intensity ratios
span_chunk: Bulk cytoplasmic pH of each Salmonella living cell expressing pHluorin(M153R) and local cytoplasmic pH of cells expressing pHluorin(M153R)-Flk or pHluorin(M153R)-MinD MTS were determined from the ratio of the fluorescence intensity in the 410-nm and 470-nm excitation wavelength images.

task_name: Prepare calibration curves for pH determination
description: Measure the 410/470 ratio of purified pHluorin(M153R)-FliG-His at different pH values to prepare the calibration curve for pH determination.
goal: to create a standard reference for accurately determining pH values from fluorescence ratios
span_chunk: The 410/470 ratio of purified pHluorin(M153R)-FliG-His was measured by our pH imaging system at different pH values to prepare the calibration curve.

task_name: Perform in vivo calibration of pH imaging system
description: Transform a Salmonella flhDC deletion strain with pYVM008, suspend the transformants in motility buffer at various external pH values, and measure intracellular pH values under the pH imaging system.
goal: to calibrate the pH imaging system with living cells at known pH conditions
span_chunk: For in vivo calibration, SJW1368, which is a Salmonella flhDC deletion strain that cannot express any flagellar genes, was transformed with pYVM008, and then, the resulting transformants were suspended in the motility buffer at various external pH values in the presence of 20 µM gramicidin and 20 mM potassium benzoate, and intracellular pH values were measured under our pH imaging system.

task_name: Prepare plant materials and growth conditions
description: Sow seeds of Phaseolus vulgaris genotypes in vermiculite, grow in a growth chamber with specific temperature, light, and humidity conditions, and cultivate seedlings in plastic pots until the primary leaves are fully-expanded.
goal: to obtain healthy common bean seedlings at the appropriate developmental stage for inoculation
span_chunk: Seeds were sown in vermiculite and grown in a growth chamber at 23°C under a 16 h light/8 h dark cycle and 75% relative humidity. Seedlings were cultivated in plastic pots filled with moist vermiculite during 10–12 days (the stage at which primary leaves are fully-expanded).

description: Transplant three seedlings into a 20 cm plastic pot with moist vermiculite and place them in a dark room 24 hours prior to inoculation.
goal: to prepare the common bean seedlings for the viral inoculation procedure
span_chunk: Three seedlings were then transplanted in moist vermiculite in a 20 cm plastic pot and placed in a dark room 24 h prior to inoculation.

task_name: Prepare DNA-plasmid mix for primary inoculation
description: Create a mix of BPMV RNA1 and RNA2 plasmids in potassium phosphate buffer for the primary inoculation of common bean leaves.
goal: to generate the inoculum for the primary infection of common bean with BPMV
span_chunk: For primary inoculation, a DNA-plasmid mix was prepared in 20 μL using 50 mM potassium phosphate buffer, pH 7.0 (=mock buffer).

task_name: Prepare leaf sap for secondary inoculations
description: Grind an infected leaf of P. vulgaris cv. Black Valentine in mock buffer to produce leaf sap for secondary inoculations.
goal: to create an inoculum from an infected plant for secondary infections
span_chunk: For secondary inoculations, an infected leaf of P. vulgaris cv. Black Valentine (fresh leaf or frozen leaf conserved at −80°C) was ground in a mortar with mock buffer to make leaf sap.

description: Inoculate common bean seedlings by mechanically rubbing one primary leaf with the prepared DNA-plasmid mix or leaf sap following a specific procedure.
goal: to introduce the BPMV into the common bean plants for infection
span_chunk: Inoculations were performed by mechanical rubbing of one primary leaf (unless otherwise stated) following the procedure described by Pflieger et al. [8].

task_name: Maintain inoculated plants under controlled conditions
description: Allow the inoculated plants to grow at 19°C under a 16 h light/8 h dark cycle in a growth chamber.
goal: to provide optimal conditions for BPMV infection and expression in common bean plants
span_chunk: The inoculated plants were allowed to grow at 19°C under a 16 h light/8 h dark cycle in a growth chamber.

description: Synthesize desthiobiotin derivatives of thiazole orange acetate TO1-Dtb and TO3-Dtb using TO1-acetate and TO3-acetate, respectively, with EZ link amine PEG 4 desthiobiotin as precursors.
goal: to obtain TO1-Dtb and TO3-Dtb for use in affinity purification
span_chunk: Synthesis of desthiobiotin derivatives of thiazole orange acetate TO1 PEG 4 desthiobiotin (TO1-Dtb) and TO3 PEG 4 desthiobiotin (TO3-Dtb) were synthesized using TO1-acetate and TO3-acetate, respectively, together with EZ link amine PEG 4 desthiobiotin (Thermo Fisher) as precursors following an established protocol.

task_name: Prepare TO1-Dtb derivatized streptavidin agarose affinity resin
description: Wash streptavidin agarose beads and incubate with TO1-Dtb to create a derivatized resin for affinity purification.
goal: to prepare the affinity resin for capturing RNA Mango tagged native RNA-protein complexes
span_chunk: Preparation of TO1-Dtb derivatized streptavidin agarose affinity resin In all experiments, streptavidin agarose beads (Invitrogen) were used for batch purification in either 1.7 mL or 5 mL tubes, as required, and solutions containing the beads were mixed using a rotator. The beads (400 µL) were washed twice with 0.1 M NaOH and 0.05 M NaCl (Buffer A) as per the manufacturer's protocol and three times with 15 mM HEPES pH 7.5, 90 mM KCl (Buffer B). TO1-Dtb was added (22.5 nmol) in 400 µL Buffer B and incubated with the washed beads for 15 min at RT.

description: Grow yeast strains, select transformants, and prepare whole-cell extracts using the liquid nitrogen method and a ball mill.
goal: to obtain yeast whole-cell extracts containing RNA Mango tagged native RNA-protein complexes
span_chunk: Yeast whole-cell extracts were prepared from strains yAAH1204 and yAAH1362 as previously described using the liquid N2 method and a ball mill.

description: Incubate yeast whole-cell extracts with TO1-Dtb saturated agarose beads, wash, and elute the snRNP with biotin.
goal: to purify RNA Mango tagged U1 M-associated snRNPs from cellular extracts
span_chunk: Pull-down of U1 M-associated snRNPs Yeast whole-cell extracts (500 µL of extract either with or without SNAP label) were added to 200 µL of TO1-Dtb saturated agarose beads and incubated at 4°C for 1 h in a rotator. The beads were washed twice each with 5 mL Buffer B for 15 min at 4°C. The beads were washed once more with buffer B at 30°C for 5 min. The snRNP was then eluted by the addition of 200 µL Buffer B supplemented with 20 mM biotin (Sigma-Aldrich) at 37°C for 30 min.

description: Prepare stock solutions of IAA, NAA, and K-NAA for use in auxin-mediated protein degradation experiments.
goal: to create concentrated solutions of auxin compounds for subsequent dilution and application in experiments
span_chunk: For IAA and NAA experiments on plates, a 250 mM stock solution in 95% ethanol was prepared using powder IAA purchased from Alfa Aesar (A10556) and powder NAA purchased from Sigma-Aldrich (317918) and stored at -20°. For K-NAA experiments on plates, a 250 mM stock solution in deionized water was prepared using powder K-NAA purchased from PhytoTechnology Laboratories (N610) and stored at 4°.

description: Dilute IAA or NAA into NGM agar at the time of pouring plates for use in auxin-mediated protein degradation experiments.
goal: to incorporate auxin into the growth medium for C. elegans to facilitate protein degradation
span_chunk: IAA or NAA was diluted into the NGM agar (cooled to approximately 50°) at the time of pouring plates.

task_name: Seed NGM Agar Plates with E. coli
description: Seed NGM agar plates with fresh OP50 E. coli for C. elegans feeding and auxin-mediated protein degradation experiments.
goal: to provide a food source for C. elegans on the NGM agar plates containing auxin
span_chunk: Fresh OP50 was used to seed plates.

task_name: Transfer Synchronized L1 Larvae to NGM Plates
description: Transfer synchronized L1 larval stage animals to standard NGM agar plates seeded with E. coli OP50.
goal: to initiate the growth and development of C. elegans for subsequent auxin treatment
span_chunk: For all auxin experiments, synchronized L1 larval stage animals were first transferred to standard nematode growth media (NGM) agar plates seeded with E. coli OP50.

description: Transfer animals at the P6.p 2-cell stage (mid-L3 stage) to NGM agar plates treated with IAA, NAA, or K-NAA.
goal: to expose C. elegans to auxin for protein degradation at a specific developmental stage
span_chunk: then transferred at the P6.p 2-cell stage (mid-L3 stage) to either OP50-seeded NGM agar plates treated with IAA, NAA, or K-NAA.

description: Conduct experiments in M9 buffer containing NAA with or without E. coli NA22, or K-NAA with E. coli NA22, in the absence of bacteria.
goal: to assess the effect of auxin on protein degradation in a liquid environment
span_chunk: Prior to each NAA experiment in M9 buffer, a fresh 1 mM (pH of 7.22) or 4 mM solution (pH of 8.14) in M9 buffer was prepared using NAA purchased in liquid form from Sigma-Aldrich (N1641).

description: Capture images of C. elegans at various time points post-auxin treatment to assess protein degradation.
goal: to visualize and quantify the protein degradation process in response to auxin treatment
span_chunk: To quantify AC- or VPC-specific degradation of AID::GFP, images were captured at the P6.p 2-cell stage and 4-cell stage (mid-L3 stage) at time points 0, 30, 60, 90, and 120 min in the absence or presence of auxin.

description: Measure the mean fluorescence intensity (MFI) of GFP-tagged proteins in C. elegans to quantify auxin-mediated degradation.
goal: to determine the extent of protein degradation by comparing fluorescence intensity at different time points
span_chunk: Expression of eft-3> AID::GFP was quantified by measuring the mean fluorescence intensity (MFI) of ACs and VPCs subtracted by the MFI of a background region in the image to account for camera noise.

description: Collect xylem exudate from Arabidopsis plants to analyze the presence and translocation of CLE peptides.
goal: to collect xylem exudate for peptide analysis
span_chunk: To explore whether the Arabidopsis CLE peptide is translocated from roots to shoots via the xylem, we collected Arabidopsis xylem exudate

description: Use nano-liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry to analyze the collected xylem exudate for the presence of mature CLE2 peptide.
goal: to detect and confirm the presence of CLE2 peptide in xylem exudate
span_chunk: we collected Arabidopsis xylem exudate and performed nano-liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (nano-LC-MS/MS) analysis

description: Analyze the MS/MS spectrum of the detected peak to match the fragmentation pattern with that of the known 12-amino acid arabinosylated CLE2 peptide.
goal: to validate the identity of the CLE2 peptide
span_chunk: The MS/MS spectrum of this peak showed a fragmentation pattern coinciding with that of the 12-amino acid arabinosylated CLE2 peptide

description: Isolate genomic DNA from Arabidopsis plants to be used for in-gel hybridization.
goal: to obtain purified DNA for subsequent analysis of telomeric G-overhangs
span_chunk: To directly assay for telomere resection, we compared the relative G-overhang size in stn1 and exo1 stn1 plants by the in gel hybridization technique.

description: Carry out the in-gel hybridization technique to detect and compare the relative size of G-overhangs in the DNA samples.
goal: to visualize and compare the extent of telomere resection in different Arabidopsis mutants
span_chunk: To directly assay for telomere resection, we compared the relative G-overhang size in stn1 and exo1 stn1 plants by the in gel hybridization technique.

description: Measure the intensity of the G-overhang signal from the in-gel hybridization to quantify the level of telomere resection.
goal: to quantify the extent of telomere resection in different Arabidopsis mutants
span_chunk: We observed a ∼6 fold increase in G-overhang signal in both mutants, showing that the excessive single-strandedness of telomeres in STN1-deficient plants is not due to EXO1.

description: Obtain CD90.2 and CD45 antibodies for intravascular and intranasal administration respectively.
goal: to label CD4+ T cells in mouse lungs by their location
span_chunk: To discriminate between cells localized to the airway versus those in the parenchyma and vasculature, we used a modification of a previously described method to simultaneously label cells by i.v. and i.n. administration of CD90.2 and CD45 antibodies, respectively.

description: Inject CD90.2 antibody intravascularly to label CD4+ T cells in the vasculature of the respiratory tract.
goal: to label CD4+ T cells in the vasculature for identification
span_chunk: To discriminate between cells localized to the airway versus those in the parenchyma and vasculature, we used a modification of a previously described method to simultaneously label cells by i.v. and i.n. administration of CD90.2 and CD45 antibodies, respectively.

description: Deliver CD45 antibody intranasally to label CD4+ T cells in the airway.
goal: to label CD4+ T cells in the airway for identification
span_chunk: To discriminate between cells localized to the airway versus those in the parenchyma and vasculature, we used a modification of a previously described method to simultaneously label cells by i.v. and i.n. administration of CD90.2 and CD45 antibodies, respectively.

description: Examine the labeled CD4+ T cells to determine their localization within the respiratory tract.
goal: to distinguish between CD4+ T cells in the airway, parenchyma, and vasculature
span_chunk: Consistent with CD8+ T cell studies, a large proportion of CD4+ T cells in the respiratory tract were localized in the vasculature. Additionally, the vast majority of cells in the airway were not labeled by i.v. antibody administration, indicating their anatomic compartmentalization.

description: Carry out the spheroid invasion assays using modifications of a previously described method.
goal: to assess cell invasion capabilities
span_chunk: Spheroid invasion assays were carried out using modifications of a previously described method.

description: Formalin-fix and paraffin-embed the spheroids for sectioning.
goal: to prepare spheroids for histological analysis
span_chunk: Spheroids were formalin-fixed/paraffin-embedded.

description: Cut 5 µm sections of the embedded spheroids and stain with haematoxylin/eosin or treat for immunohistochemistry.
goal: to visualize spheroid structure and invasion
span_chunk: 5 µm sections stained with haematoxylin/eosin, or treated for immunohistochemistry.

description: Electroporate pronuclear-stage embryos with Cas9-RNP to facilitate gene editing.
goal: to facilitate CRISPR/Cas9-mediated gene editing in embryos
span_chunk: After introducing the Cas9-RNP into pronuclear-stage embryos by electroporation

description: Infect the electroporated embryos with a self-complementary AAV (scAAV) vector containing the gene cassette for knockin.
goal: to deliver donor DNA into embryos for gene knockin
span_chunk: we infected with a self-complementary AAV (scAAV) vector harboring a 1.8-kb CAG-GFP cassette flanked by two 100-bp Rosa26 homology arms

task_name: Assess knockin efficiency at blastocyst stage
description: Evaluate the efficiency of gene knockin in the Rosa26 locus at the blastocyst stage.
goal: to determine the success rate of gene knockin
span_chunk: At the blastocyst stage, the efficiency of knockin in the Rosa26 locus was 15.5%

description: Use fluorescence stereomicroscopy and flow cytometry to confirm the expression of the EGFP reporter gene.
goal: to verify successful gene knockin and expression
span_chunk: EGFP expression was confirmed by fluorescence stereomicroscopy and flow cytometry of peripheral blood

description: Check for correct insertion of the gene cassette in the Rosa26 locus without indel mutations at the site of junction.
goal: to ensure precise gene knockin without unintended mutations
span_chunk: the cassette was correctly inserted in the Rosa26 locus without indel mutations at the site of junction

description: Breed knockin founders with wild-type mice and genotype N1 generation offspring to confirm germline transmission of the knockin allele.
goal: to establish stable germline transmission of the knockin allele
span_chunk: Germline transmission was confirmed by breeding the knockin founders and wild-type C57BL/6N mice, followed by genotyping of N1 generation offsprings

description: K562 cells cultured in RPMI medium are fixed with 1% formaldehyde and the crosslink is quenched with 125 mM glycine.
goal: to stabilize the chromatin structure for subsequent immunoprecipitation
span_chunk: K562 cells cultured in RPMI medium (supplemented with 10% Fetal Bovine Serum), at 37°C and 5% CO2, were fixed for 10 min at room temperature with 1% formaldehyde. The crosslink was quenched with 125 mM glycine.

description: Fixed K562 cells are sorted on a BD FACSAria cell sorter using Hoechst stain to obtain a pure population.
goal: to isolate a specific population of cells for ChIP-Seq
span_chunk: sorted on BD FACSAria cell sorter using Hoechst stain.

description: Sorted cells are sonicated with three cycles at low power settings to break the nuclei.
goal: to fragment the chromatin for tagmentation
span_chunk: sonicated with three cycles at low power settings for breaking the nuclei.

description: Protein A and G Dynabeads are coupled to a specific antibody in blocking buffer for 2-3 hours at 4°C.
goal: to prepare the beads for chromatin immunoprecipitation
span_chunk: 15 μl of Protein A and G Dynabeads were coupled to 1 μg of specific antibody in the blocking buffer for 2-3 h at 4°C.

description: The partially fragmented chromatin is incubated overnight with antibody-coupled beads at 4°C with head-over-tail rotations.
goal: to capture the chromatin fragments of interest
span_chunk: The partially fragmented chromatin was centrifuged at 2,000 g for 10 min at 4°C, and the supernatant was transferred to the tube with blocked and antibody-coupled beads.

description: The washed beads with chromatin are resuspended in tagmentation DNA buffer containing Nextera DNA tagmentation enzyme and incubated at 37°C for 40 min with shaking.
goal: to fragment and tag the DNA for sequencing
span_chunk: The washed beads were resupended in 20 μl of 1× tagmentation DNA buffer containing 1 μl of Nextera DNA tagmentation enzyme and incubated at 37°C for 40 min with constant shaking.

task_name: Proteinase K treatment and DNA purification
description: The tagmented samples are treated with proteinase K and then subjected to phenol-chloroform extraction or direct PCR amplification after deactivating proteinase K.
goal: to reverse cross-links and purify the DNA
span_chunk: The samples were subjected to proteinase K treatment in 50 μl of TE buffer, pH 8.0, with 5 μl of 20 mg/ml of proteinase K for overnight at 60°C in thermoblock with shaking at 500 rpm.

description: The DNA is amplified using NEBNext High-Fidelity PCR Mix with primers containing molecular indices, followed by bead-based size selection.
goal: to enrich and select the DNA fragments for sequencing
span_chunk: The DNA was amplified in 100 μl reaction with 1X NEBNext High-Fidelity PCR Mix with 0.4 μM of primers containing molecular indices.

description: The PCR-amplified DNA is purified, analyzed for size distribution, quantified, pooled, and sequenced on an Illumina NextSeq 500.
goal: to generate sequencing data for ChIP-Seq analysis
span_chunk: The finished libraries were pooled in equimolar amounts and sequenced on Illumina NextSeq 500.

task_name: Prepare PDMS chamber for tissue compression
description: Expose the PDMS chamber to plasma arc for hydrophilic treatment and place isolated epididymides onto the chamber in its 50% stretched state.
goal: to enhance adhesion between the chamber and collagen gel
span_chunk: First, we exposed the PDMS chamber to plasma arc for 1 min using a desktop vacuum plasma processing device for hydrophilic treatment to enhance the adhesion between the chamber and collagen gel into which the epididymides were embedded.

description: Fill the hydrophilized PDMS chamber with type I collagen and allow gelation to embed the epididymides.
goal: to embed the epididymides for compression assay
span_chunk: Next, we immediately placed isolated epididymides onto the hydrophilized PDMS chamber in its 50% stretched state, and filled the chamber with 500 μl of type I collagen, followed by gelation for 10 min at 37°C.

description: Compress the epididymides with collagen gel by relaxing the chamber from the 50% stretched state at a controlled speed.
goal: to apply mechanical compression to the tissue
span_chunk: Then, the epididymides with the collagen gel were compressed by relaxing from the 50% stretched state around 0.2 mm/s.

description: Incubate the compressed samples for a specific time for morphological confirmation or western blotting analysis.
goal: to allow for morphological changes or protein expression analysis post-compression
span_chunk: Finally, the samples were incubated for 10 min for the morphological confirmation analysis and 20 min for the western blotting analysis at 37°C under 5% CO2.

description: Analyze the morphology of the compressed tissue after incubation to assess the effects of compression.
goal: to evaluate the impact of compression on tissue structure
span_chunk: Finally, the samples were incubated for 10 min for the morphological confirmation analysis and 20 min for the western blotting analysis at 37°C under 5% CO2.

description: Extract total protein from the compressed tissue and perform western blotting to analyze protein expression.
goal: to assess changes in protein expression due to tissue compression
span_chunk: For the western blotting analysis, we extracted total protein from each treatment, and adjusted the amount such that it was the same across treatments for SDS-PAGE as described in the next section.

task_name: Adoptive transfer of OT-II or OT-I T cells
description: Wild-type B6 mice were adoptively transferred with 3 × 10^6 OT-II or OT-I T cells the day before the in vivo priming assay.
goal: to prepare recipient mice for in vivo priming with pulsed dendritic cells
span_chunk: Wild-type B6 mice were adoptively transferred with 3 × 10^6 OT-II or OT-I T cells the day before.

task_name: Injection of OVA-pulsed BM-DCcons and iPS-DCregs
description: OVA-pulsed B6 BM-DCcons combined with iPS-DCregs were injected subcutaneously into the recipients' footpads.
goal: to prime T cells in vivo with in vitro pulsed dendritic cells
span_chunk: OVA-pulsed B6 BM-DCcons (1.5 × 10^5) combined with iPS-DCregs or other controls (3 × 10^5) were injected subcutaneously into the recipients' footpads.

task_name: Isolation of OVA-specific reactive T cells from PLNs
description: Following the in vivo priming, OVA-specific reactive T cells were isolated from the popliteal lymph nodes (PLNs) of the recipient mice.
goal: to assess the proliferation response of T cells after in vivo priming
span_chunk: The OVA-specific reactive T cells isolated from the PLNs were intensely proliferated in the BM-DCcons and iPS-DCcons groups, but were significantly inhibited in the BM-DCregs and iPS-DCregs groups.

task_name: Isolate Plasma Cells from Synovial Fluid
description: Plasma cells are obtained from the synovial fluid of a patient with anti‐CCP–positive RA, and antibody‐secreting cells are isolated using the fluorescent foci method.
goal: to obtain plasma cells capable of secreting antibodies specific to citrulline
span_chunk: Plasma cells were obtained from the synovial fluid of a patient with anti‐CCP–positive RA, and antibody‐secreting cells were isolated from synovial fluid mononuclear cells using the fluorescent foci method.

task_name: Sort Citrulline-specific B Cells by Flow Cytometry
description: Single citrulline‐specific B cells are sorted from the peripheral blood of RA patients using an antigen‐tetramer system.
goal: to isolate B cells that are specific to citrulline for monoclonal antibody production
span_chunk: In addition, single citrulline‐specific B cells were sorted by flow cytometry from the peripheral blood of other RA patients, using an antigen‐tetramer system.

description: Conduct ELISA to assess binding of monoclonal antibodies to citrulline-containing and arginine-containing peptides.
goal: to evaluate the specificity of monoclonal antibodies to citrulline
span_chunk: Peptide ELISAs were performed as previously described 20, with some minor modifications. The ELISAs assessed binding to both citrulline‐containing and arginine (Arg)–containing peptides.

description: Perform ELISA using full-length proteins coated on plates, followed by citrullination and incubation with ACPAs and secondary antibodies.
goal: to determine the reactivity of ACPAs to citrullinated full-length proteins
span_chunk: For the full‐length protein ELISA, 10 μg/ml of fibrinogen, recombinant vimentin, and histone H4 were diluted in PBS and coated on Nunc Maxisorp 96‐well plates.

task_name: Scan with Extracellular Matrix Peptide Microarray
description: Use a microarray containing peptides from extracellular matrix proteins to scan for reactivity with monoclonal antibodies.
goal: to identify citrulline and homocitrulline reactivity profiles of monoclonal antibodies
span_chunk: Scanning for citrulline and homocitrulline reactivity with each mAb was performed at a resolution of 2 μm, using a NimbleGen MS200 Scanner (Roche NimbleGen).

description: Design and clone cDNAs encoding FLAG-tagged proteins and human VHL into pBABED-Puro vectors for constitutive expression.
goal: to create plasmids for the expression of AdPROM components
span_chunk: The cDNAs encoding FLAG-aNSa1 (DU54816), FLAG-VHL-aNSa1 (DU54843), FLAG-aCS3 (DU54817), FLAG-VHL-aCS3 (DU54844), FLAG-aASC (DU54821), FLAG-VHL-aASC (DU54832) and human VHL (DU54023) were designed from published protein sequences and cloned into pBABED-Puro vectors for constitutive expression.

description: Co-transfect pBABED retroviral plasmids with pCMV-gag-pol and pCMV-VSV-G in 293-FT cells to produce retroviruses for AdPROM expression.
goal: to generate retroviruses for infecting target cells with AdPROM constructs
span_chunk: For retroviral production, pBABED retroviral plasmids encoding appropriate proteins were co-transfected with pCMV-gag-pol and pCMV-VSV-G in a 10 cm–diameter dish of 70% confluent 293-FT cells.

description: Infect approximately 60% confluent target cells with the optimized titre of retroviral medium containing polybrene for 24 hours.
goal: to introduce AdPROM constructs into target cells for protein expression
span_chunk: Target cells (approx. 60% confluent) were infected with the optimized titre of retroviral medium containing 8 µg ml −1 polybrene (Sigma) for 24 h.

description: Select cells that have integrated the retrovirus by treating with puromycin.
goal: to isolate cells that have successfully incorporated the AdPROM constructs
span_chunk: Cells which had integrated the retrovirus were selected with 2 µg ml −1 puromycin thereafter.

task_name: Lyse cells and prepare protein extracts
description: Wash cells with PBS, lyse in buffer with protease inhibitors and β-mercaptoethanol, clarify extracts, and determine protein concentration.
goal: to obtain protein extracts from cells expressing AdPROM constructs
span_chunk: For lysis, cells were washed twice in ice-cold phosphate-buffered saline (PBS), scraped on ice in lysis buffer supplemented with complete protease inhibitors and 0.1% (v/v) β-mercaptoethanol (Sigma). Cell extracts were clarified and either processed immediately or snap-frozen in liquid nitrogen prior to storage at −80°C.

description: Incubate lysates with anti-FLAG M2 resin overnight at 4°C, wash, and elute FLAG-fusion proteins by boiling in SDS sample buffer.
goal: to isolate AdPROM components from the protein extracts
span_chunk: For anti-FLAG M2 immunoprecipitation, lysates (typically 1 mg) were incubated with anti-FLAG M2 resin (10 µl) for 16 h overnight at 4°C on a rotating wheel. Following washing of the resin with lysis buffer 3×, FLAG-fusion proteins were eluted from the resin by boiling for 5 min at 95°C in 1× SDS sample buffer.

task_name: Analyze proteins by SDS-PAGE and western blotting
description: Separate proteins on SDS-PAGE gels, transfer to membranes, block, incubate with primary and secondary antibodies, and detect using ECL reagent.
goal: to analyze the expression and targeted destruction of endogenous proteins by AdPROM
span_chunk: Reduced protein extracts or immunoprecipitates were separated on SDS-PAGE gels, transferred onto membranes, blocked, incubated with primary and secondary antibodies, and detected using enhanced chemiluminescence (ECL) reagent.

description: Protoplasts are isolated from petunia petals using a previously described method by Faraco et al. (2014), ensuring cell viability with fluorescein diacetate staining and microscopic observation.
goal: to obtain a population of viable protoplasts from petunia petals
span_chunk: Protoplasts were isolated from petunia petals (line Blue Ray) as described by Faraco et al. (2014). Protoplast viability was assayed by incubating cells with 50 μg/ml fluorescein diacetate solution (Sigma Aldrich) in a 1:1 mixture (v/v) for 5 min prior to observation under the microscope.

description: Intact vacuoles are isolated from the protoplasts using an osmotic and thermal lysis method followed by separation with a Ficoll step gradient centrifugation.
goal: to separate and collect intact vacuoles from lysed protoplasts
span_chunk: Intact vacuoles were isolated from protoplasts as described previously (Robert et al., 2007) with some modifications. Briefly, protoplasts were osmotically and thermally lysed, and the vacuole fraction was separated from the lysate using a Ficoll step gradient in 15-ml tubes.

description: The purity of the isolated vacuoles is assessed using light microscopy and western blot analysis to ensure the fraction is free from other cellular components.
goal: to confirm the purity of the isolated vacuole fraction
span_chunk: Vacuole purity was evaluated using light microscopy and western blot analysis.

task_name: Extract glycosides from protoplasts and vacuoles
description: Glycosylated scent compounds are extracted from the protoplasts and vacuoles using a methanol:water solution, sonication, and enzymatic hydrolysis, followed by hexane extraction.
goal: to obtain glycosylated phenylpropanoid compounds from protoplasts and vacuoles
span_chunk: Extraction of glycosides from protoplasts and vacuoles and their quantitation by GC–MS were performed as above.

description: The extracted glycosides are quantitated using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC–MS) to determine the concentration of glycosylated scent compounds.
goal: to measure the amount of glycosylated scent compounds present in the samples
span_chunk: Extraction of glycosides from protoplasts and vacuoles and their quantitation by GC–MS were performed as above.

description: Set up a modified Barnes maze with 40 escape holes, visual cues, and a dark escape tube at the designated escape hole.
goal: to create the environment for the DMP dry maze test
span_chunk: we used a modified Barnes maze with 40 escape holes (D = 5 cm, 16 holes on the outer ring with 50-cm distance to the center, 16 holes on the middle ring with 35-cm distance to the center, and 8 holes on the inner ring with 20-cm distance to the center). All holes were uncovered with the exception of the escape hole, which is covered with a dark escape tube (a black PVC tube).

description: Adjust the light to approximately 1200 lux and set up a noise source at 2 kHz, 85 dB to be used during the test.
goal: to ensure consistent sensory stimuli during the DMP dry maze test
span_chunk: The light was set to approximately 1200 lux, and a noise (2 kHz, 85 dB) was used during the test.

description: Place mice at the center of the maze under a dark box for 30 seconds, then start the trial by removing the box and end it when mice find the escape hole within 90 seconds.
goal: to measure spatial working memory of the mice
span_chunk: Mice were giving four trials each day with interval of 10 min. Mice were placed at the center of the maze under a dark box for 30 s. The trial started when the box was removed and ended when the mice found the escape hole within 90 s.

task_name: Guide Mice to Escape Hole if Necessary
description: If a mouse cannot find the escape hole within 90 seconds, guide it to the hole.
goal: to ensure each mouse completes the trial
span_chunk: Mice were guided to the escape hole by the experimenter if they could not find it within 90 s.

task_name: Clean Maze Surface and Escape Tube
description: After each trial, clean the maze surface and the escape tube with 70% ethanol to minimize odor cues.
goal: to prevent mice from using olfactory cues to solve the maze
span_chunk: The maze surface and the escape tube were cleaned with 70% ethanol (v/v) after each trial to minimize odor cues.

description: Use an overhead camera to record the trials and analyze them with Ethovision software.
goal: to track and evaluate the performance of mice in the DMP dry maze test
span_chunk: Trials were recorded by an overhead camera and analyzed by Ethovision (Ethovision, Noldus).

description: Viral RNA was extracted from virus culture supernatants or patients' plasma using the QIAamp Viral Min Kit.
goal: to obtain purified viral RNA for the RT-LAMP assay
span_chunk: Viral RNA was extracted from 140 μl virus culture supernatants or patients' plasma using the QIAamp Viral Min Kit (Qiagen, Germany).

description: A reaction mix was prepared including isothermal amplification buffer, MgSO4, dNTPs, Bst 2.0 DNA polymerase, WarmStart RT, Q5 High-Fidelity DNA Polymerase, and various primers.
goal: to set up the novel mismatch-tolerant RT-LAMP system
span_chunk: A 25 μl reaction mix of the novel RT-LAMP assay includes 1× isothermal amplification buffer, 6 mM MgSO4, 1.4 mM dNTPs, 8 units of Bst 2.0 DNA polymerase, 7.5 units of WarmStart RT, 0.15 unit of Q5 High-Fidelity DNA Polymerase, 20 pmol each of primers FIP/123, FIP/4, BIP/123, and BIP/4, 2.5 pmol each of primers F3/134, F3/2, B3/123, and B3/4, and 20 pmol of loop primer BLP/1234.

description: The RT-LAMP reaction was performed at 63°C for 60 minutes with SYTO 9 fluorescent dye for real-time monitoring.
goal: to amplify and detect viral RNA using the novel RT-LAMP method
span_chunk: The RT-LAMP reaction was performed at 63°C for 60 min with 0.4 μM SYTO 9 (Life technologies, Carlsbad, CA, United States) as fluorescent dye for real-time monitoring by the Light Cycler 96 real-time PCR System (Roche Diagnostics, Mannheim, Germany).

task_name: Determine Sensitivity and Limit of Detection
description: Ten-fold serial dilutions of RNA from four DENV stocks were used to determine the sensitivity and LOD of the RT-LAMP assay, with additional experiments using fivefold dilutions.
goal: to establish the sensitivity and LOD for the novel DENV RT-LAMP assay
span_chunk: Ten-fold serial dilution of the RNA from four DENV stocks were used as the standards to determine the sensitivity of the novel DENV RT-LAMP assay... LOD of the novel DENV RT-LAMP assay was determined using 10-fold serial dilutions of RNA from each virus stock.

description: Probit regression analysis was performed using SPSS 17.0 software to more accurately estimate the LOD.
goal: to calculate the 95% probability of obtaining a positive result for the LOD
span_chunk: Probit regression analysis was performed to determine the LOD using the SPSS 17.0 software.

description: Express a FLAG-tagged isoform of TBPH in Drosophila neurons for subsequent immunoprecipitation.
goal: to obtain TBPH protein for pull-down assays
span_chunk: For these experiments, we expressed a FLAG-tagged isoform of TBPH in Drosophila neurons and performed pull-down assays from fly head tissues.

description: Carry out immunoprecipitation using anti-FLAG antibodies to isolate TBPH protein complexes from Drosophila head tissues.
goal: to isolate TBPH protein complexes for analysis
span_chunk: For these experiments, we expressed a FLAG-tagged isoform of TBPH in Drosophila neurons and performed pull-down assays from fly head tissues.

task_name: Analyze RNA enrichment in TBPH immunoprecipitates
description: Assess the enrichment of Dcr-2 mRNA in the TBPH immunoprecipitated samples compared to controls.
goal: to confirm the physical interaction between TBPH and Dcr-2 mRNA
span_chunk: In this manner, we found that the mRNA of Dcr-2 appeared highly enriched in TBPH immunoprecipitated samples compared to similar experiments performed utilizing a modified variant of this protein that is unable to bind the RNA (TBPH-RBD mut), confirming that these molecules physically interact in vivo.

task_name: Analyze protein-protein interactions in TBPH immunoprecipitates
description: Investigate the interaction between TBPH and Dcr-2 at the protein level within the immunoprecipitated samples.
goal: to demonstrate that TBPH and Dcr-2 form part of the same protein complex
span_chunk: In addition, we observed that TBPH was also capable to interact with Dcr-2 at the protein level demonstrating that these molecules form part of the same protein complex in Drosophila neurons.

description: Culture synovial fibroblasts from patients with RA and OA, as well as human dermal fibroblasts, for use in migration assays.
goal: to obtain viable fibroblast cultures for migration analysis
span_chunk: RA-derived and osteoarthritis (OA)-derived synovial fibroblasts as well as human dermal fibroblasts were used in cell culture experiments.

description: Wash the cells with phosphate buffered saline and starve them for 2 hours in medium without fetal bovine serum.
goal: to induce a starvation state in fibroblast cultures
span_chunk: When indicated, the cells were washed with phosphate buffered saline and starved for 2 hours in medium without fetal bovine serum.

task_name: Pretreat cells with proteins and antibodies
description: Add citrullinated or native human purified fibrinogen, recombinant vimentin, α-enolase, and histone H4 as pretreatment to ACPA and control IgGs at 4°C overnight.
goal: to expose fibroblasts to specific proteins and antibodies before migration assay
span_chunk: Citrullinated or native human purified fibrinogen, recombinant vimentin, α-enolase and histone H4 were added as pretreatment to ACPA and control IgGs at 4°C overnight.

task_name: Perform live cell imaging for migration
