description: Assess fibroblast migration using the IncuCyte Zoom live cell imaging system.
goal: to dynamically analyze the migration of adherent fibroblasts
span_chunk: Fibroblast migration was assessed by IncuCyte Zoom live cell imaging system or by scratch assay.

description: Perform a scratch assay to evaluate fibroblast migration in a static manner.
goal: to assess the migration capacity of fibroblasts after treatment
span_chunk: Fibroblast migration was assessed by IncuCyte Zoom live cell imaging system or by scratch assay.

description: Infect N2 worms with fungal spores on NGMY plates, incubate, transfer to NGMY liquid medium, culture, and collect mycelia by filtration for protoplast preparation.
goal: to obtain Drechmeria coniospora protoplasts for transformation
span_chunk: N2 worms at the L4 stage were infected with fungal spores as described [ 114 ] on NGMY plates spread with the E . coli strain OP50 and incubated for 24 h, then transferred into NGMY liquid medium and cultured for another 30 h. Mycelia were collected by filtration as above and protoplasts prepared...

description: Transform the prepared protoplasts using polyethylene glycol (PEG)/CaCl2-mediated DNA uptake with expression vectors containing a hygromycin selection marker.
goal: to introduce genetic material into Drechmeria coniospora protoplasts
span_chunk: protoplasts prepared and transformed using polyethylene glycol (PEG)/CaCl2-mediated DNA uptake as described [ 137 ], using expression vectors (see S1 Methods ) containing a hygromycin selection marker...

description: Select transformants for antibiotic resistance on medium containing hygromycin and screen for fluorescence to identify successful transformations.
goal: to isolate and identify successfully transformed Drechmeria coniospora
span_chunk: Transformants were selected for antibiotic resistance on medium containing 15 μg/ml hygromycin and screened for fluorescence.

task_name: Prepare DFMA and DFMO inhibitor solution
description: Dissolve difluoromethylarginine (DFMA) and difluoromethylornithine (DFMO) in water to create an inhibitor solution containing 2mM DFMA and 5mM DFMO.
goal: to inhibit putrescine biosynthesis in tomato plants
span_chunk: The chemical PA biosynthesis inhibitors difluoromethylarginine (DFMA) and difluoromethylornithine (DFMO), obtained from Dr Altabella, Centre for Research in Agricultural Genomics (CRAG), were dissolved in water and an inhibitor solution containing 2mM DFMA and 5mM DFMO was produced.

task_name: Apply inhibitor solution to tomato plants
description: Apply the prepared inhibitor solution directly to each pot of 4-week-old tomato plants during the week prior to Pseudomonas syringae (Pst) inoculation.
goal: to treat tomato plants with PA biosynthesis inhibitors
span_chunk: Four treatments were performed, with the inhibitor solution was applied directly to each pot during the week prior to Pst inoculation.

task_name: Treat plants with Putrescine or mock solution
description: Treat 4-week-old tomato plants with 0.5mM Putrescine (Put) or mock solution (water) using foliar sprays applied 48 hours before Pst infection.
goal: to compare the effect of Putrescine treatment with mock treatment
span_chunk: For Put treatment, 4-week-old plants were treated with 0.5mM Put or mock solution (water) using foliar sprays applied 48h before Pst infection.

task_name: Maintain treated plants under controlled conditions
description: Keep the treated tomato plants in the same culture conditions as described for growth and nutrition treatments.
goal: to ensure consistent environmental conditions for treated plants
span_chunk: Tomato plants were maintained in the same culture conditions and inoculated as described above.

description: Sacrifice DSS-treated mice by CO2 euthanasia and collect a small piece (50 mg) of proximal colon for RNA extraction.
goal: to obtain tissue samples for RNA extraction
span_chunk: After 7 days under DSS treatment, the mice were sacrificed by CO2 euthanasia. A small piece (50 mg) of proximal colon was taken for RNA extraction.

description: Isolate total RNA from the collected colonic tissues using TRIzol reagent according to the manufacturer's instructions.
goal: to extract total RNA from tissue samples
span_chunk: Total RNA was isolated from colonic tissues using TRIzol (Life Technologies, Carlsbad, CA) according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

description: Incubate RNA with 8 M LiCl on ice, centrifuge to collect RNA pellet, and repeat the process for further purification.
goal: to purify RNA from polysaccharides including DSS
span_chunk: The RNA were incubated with 0.1 volume of 8 M LiCl diluted in RNase-free water on ice for 2 h and then centrifuged at 14,000 g for 30 min at 4°C. The supernatants were poured out and the pellets of RNA dissolved in 200 μl of RNase-free water. The 2-hour incubation with lithium chloride, the centrifugation and the pellet suspensions were repeated once more.

description: Precipitate RNA at -20°C with sodium acetate and ethanol, centrifuge, wash the pellet with ethanol, and then dissolve in RNase-free water.
goal: to precipitate and wash RNA for final purification
span_chunk: The RNA was precipitated at -20°C for 30 min, in 0.1 volume of 3 M sodium acetate (pH 5.2) and 2 volumes of 100% absolute ethanol. The RNA was then centrifuged at 14,000 g for 30 min at 4°C. The supernatants were poured out and the pellets were washed with 100 μL of 70% ethanol and centrifuged at 14,000 g for 10 min at 4°C. The supernatants were removed and the RNA was dissolved in 20–50 μl of RNase-free water.

description: Evaluate the integrity of the purified RNA by performing 2% agarose gel electrophoresis.
goal: to verify the quality of the purified RNA
span_chunk: The RNA integrity was assessed by 2% agarose gel electrophoresis.

description: Split confluent plates of 293T cells 1:4 the day before transfection to ensure optimal cell density for transfection.
goal: to ensure optimal cell density for transfection
span_chunk: Confluent plates of 293T cells were split 1:4 the day before transfection.

description: Transfect each plate of 293T cells with 1 μg gag/pol construct, 1.5 μg of enhanced GFP reporter construct, and 1.5 μg envelope-expressing construct using Fugene-6 transfection reagent.
goal: to produce viral vectors expressing the desired genes
span_chunk: Each plate of 293T cells was transfected with 1 μg gag/pol construct, 1.5 μg of enhanced GFP reporter construct, and 1.5 μg envelope-expressing construct by using the Fugene-6 transfection reagent.

task_name: Harvest and filter viral vector supernatant
description: Collect the supernatant from the transfected 293T cells at 48 h and 72 h post-transfection, filter through 0.45-μm filters, and store at –80°C.
goal: to obtain a clean preparation of viral vectors for further use
span_chunk: Supernatant was harvested 48 h and 72 h posttransfection, filtered through 0.45-μm filters, and stored at –80 o C.

description: Infect 293T, TE671, and QT6/ACE2 cells with the viral vector and determine eGFP titers 72 h later by fluorescence-activated cell sorter (FACS).
goal: to quantify the infectious units of the viral vectors
span_chunk: MLV and HIV vector titer were measured on 293T, TE671, and QT6/ACE2 cells and are presented as infectious units (IU) per milliliter.

description: Heat inactivate patient serum samples, serially dilute, mix with MLV(SARS) virions, incubate with QT6/ACE2 cells, and count GFP-positive cells 48 h later by fluorescence microscopy.
goal: to assess the neutralizing antibody response to SARS-CoV spike luciferase pseudotypes
span_chunk: Pseudotype Patient serum samples were heat inactivated at 56°C for 30 min, 2-fold serially diluted from 1:10 in culture medium, and mixed with MLV(SARS) virions (≈100 IU) at a 1:1 vol/vol ratio. After incubation at 37°C for 1 h, 100 μL of each dilution was added to QT6/ACE2 cells seeded at 1 × 10 4 cells per well in 96-well flat-bottomed tissue culture plates seeded 24 h previously. GFP-positive cells were counted 48 h later by fluorescence microscopy.

task_name: Grow Arabidopsis plants for Hpa inoculation
description: Arabidopsis plants are grown at specific temperature, humidity, and photoperiod conditions in environmentally controlled growth cabinets to prepare them for Hpa inoculation.
goal: to prepare Arabidopsis plants for Hpa infection assay
span_chunk: For Hpa -inoculation assay, Arabidopsis plants were grown at 22°C and 60% humidity under a 10-h photoperiod and a 14-h dark period in environmentally controlled growth cabinets.

task_name: Inoculate Arabidopsis plants with Hpa spores
description: Spray-inoculate Arabidopsis plants to saturation with a spore suspension of Hpa to initiate infection.
goal: to infect Arabidopsis plants with Hpa for the infection assay
span_chunk: For Hpa infection, Arabidopsis plants were spray-inoculated to saturation with a spore suspension of 5×10^4 conidiospores/ml.

description: Cover the inoculated plants with a transparent lid to maintain high humidity conditions in a growth cabinet at a specific temperature and photoperiod until the day of sampling.
goal: to provide optimal conditions for Hpa growth and infection
span_chunk: Plants were covered with a transparent lid to maintain high humidity (90–100%) conditions in a growth cabinet at 16°C under a 10-h photoperiod until the day for sampling.

task_name: Stain inoculated leaves with trypan blue
description: To evaluate hyphae growth and HR cell death, stain leaves inoculated with Hpa with trypan blue.
goal: to assess the extent of Hpa infection and host cell death
span_chunk: To evaluate hyphae growth and HR cell death, leaves inoculated with Hpa Emoy2 or Waco9 were stained with trypan blue.

description: Harvest pools of plants, release conidiospores in water, and determine the amount of conidiospores using a haemocytometer.
goal: to quantify the production of conidiospores by Hpa
span_chunk: To evaluate conidiospore production, 5 pools of 3 plants for each Arabidopsis line were harvested in 1 ml of water. After vortexing, the amount of conidiospores released was determined using a haemocytometer.

description: Seed Cor3–1 cells at 1.5 × 10^6 in 10 cm dishes and P19 cells at 1.0 × 10^6 in 10 cm dishes for cellular fractionation.
goal: to prepare cells for subsequent fractionation steps
span_chunk: Cor3–1 cells were seeded at 1.5 × 10^6 in 10 cm dishes and P19 were seeded at 1.0 × 10^6 in 10 cm dishes.

description: Wash the seeded cells once with room temperature PBS, scrape into 1 ml PBS, and pellet at 1,200 rpm in an eppendorf tube at 4°C for 3 min.
goal: to collect cells for fractionation
span_chunk: Cells were washed once with room temperature PBS and scraped into 1 ml PBS. Cells were pelleted at 1,200 rpm in an eppendorf tube at 4°C for 3 min.

description: Resuspend cell pellets in ice-cold E1 buffer with protease inhibitor, pipette gently, and centrifuge to collect the supernatant as the cytoplasm fraction.
goal: to separate the cytoplasmic components from the cells
span_chunk: Pellets were covered with 5 volumes of ice-cold E1 buffer... The supernatant was collected in a fresh tube (cytoplasm fraction).

description: Resuspend the pellet in E1 buffer, centrifuge, discard the supernatant, and then resuspend in E2 buffer with protease inhibitor to collect the supernatant as the nucleus fraction.
goal: to isolate the nuclear components from the cells
span_chunk: The supernatant was discarded and the pellet was resuspended by gentle pipetting in the same volume of E2 buffer... The supernatant was collected in a fresh tube (nucleus fraction).

description: Resuspend the pellet in E3 buffer with protease inhibitor, sonicate, and centrifuge to collect the solution as the chromatin fraction.
goal: to obtain the chromatin-bound proteins
span_chunk: The supernatant was discarded and the pellet was resuspended in ice-cold E3 buffer... The solution (chromatin fraction) was sonicated in a Bioruptor.

description: Use BCA protein assay kit to determine the protein concentration of the isolated fractions.
goal: to quantify the protein content in each fraction
span_chunk: All fractions were centrifuged at 13,000 rpm at 4°C for 10 min and protein concentration was determined using BCA protein assay kit.

description: Male albino Wistar rats were kept at constant room temperature and humidity with a 12:12-hour light–dark cycle and free access to food and water.
goal: to maintain a controlled environment for the rats prior to the stress model induction
span_chunk: The rats were kept at constant room temperature of 22°C ± 1°C and 60% relative humidity on a 12:12-hour light–dark cycle with free access to food and water.

description: Rats were anesthetized with chloral hydrate and positioned in a stereotaxic apparatus to align with brain atlas coordinates for subsequent injections.
goal: to prepare rats for precise intranigral injections
span_chunk: Rats were anaesthetized with chloral hydrate (400 mg/kg) and positioned in a stereotaxic apparatus (Kopf Instruments, Tujunga, CA, USA) to conform to the brain atlas of Paxinos and Watson.

description: Injections into the substantia nigra were made according to specific coordinates from the bregma to deliver vehicle or LPS.
goal: to administer treatments into the left substantia nigra of rats
span_chunk: Injections into the SN were made 5.5 mm posterior, 1.8 mm lateral and 8.3 mm ventral to the bregma at day 1, 2 hours after the application of the first stressor.

description: A 9-day variate stressor paradigm was used for the animals in the stressed groups, with stressors applied at different times to minimize predictability.
goal: to induce chronic variate stress in the rat model
span_chunk: A 9-day variate stressor paradigm was used for the animals in the stressed groups. The schedule of stressors is given in Table 1. Application of stress started at different times from day to day (between 08:00 and 20:00) to minimize its predictability.

description: Body weight was measured at the beginning and the end of the 10-day treatment as an indirect parameter of HPA axis activation.
goal: to assess the impact of stress on the rats' physiological response
span_chunk: Body weight was measured at the beginning and the end of the 10-day treatment and was evaluated as an indirect parameter of HPA axis activation.

description: Culture cells in DMEM with fetal bovine serum or serum-free formulations and add recombinant ribonuclease inhibitor in selected experiments.
goal: to obtain cell-conditioned medium for subsequent nonvesicular extracellular fraction preparation
span_chunk: Preparation of cell-conditioned medium Cells were cultured in DMEM + 10% fetal bovine serum (S+ medium) at 37°C and 5% CO2 or in different serum-free formulations as depicted in SI Materials and Methods.

task_name: Prepare nonvesicular extracellular fraction by ultracentrifugation
description: Centrifuge the cell-conditioned medium at 100,000 × g and concentrate the supernatant for size-exclusion chromatography or RNA extraction.
goal: to isolate the nonvesicular extracellular fraction from cell-conditioned medium
span_chunk: Preparation of the nonvesicular extracellular fraction by ultracentrifugation The cell-condtioned medium already spinned at 2000 × g was centrifuged for 2.5 h at 100 000 × g and 4°C in a Beckman Coulter Optima XPN-90 ultracentrifuge using a SW40 Ti rotor.

description: Concentrate the 100,000 × g supernatants by ultrafiltration, inject into a Superdex S200 column, and collect fractions while monitoring absorbance.
goal: to separate nonvesicular extracellular RNAs by size
span_chunk: Size exclusion chromatography The 100 000 × g supernatants of the cell-conditioned medium were concentrated by ultrafiltration by successive dilutions with PBS to remove phenol red and small molecules.

description: Use empirically determined 260/280 ratios from pure BSA and synthetic tRNA to deconvolute the chromatograms obtained from size exclusion chromatography.
goal: to analyze the size distribution of nonvesicular extracellular RNAs
span_chunk: Chromatograms were deconvoluted in silico using empirically determined 260/280 ratios from pure bovine serum albumin (BSA) and synthetic tRNA Gly GCC 5′ halves (of 30 nt).

description: Purify RNA from selected chromatographic peaks, prepare NGS libraries, and perform sequencing on a MiSeq benchtop sequencer.
goal: to identify and profile the small RNAs present in nonvesicular extracellular fractions
span_chunk: Sequencing of small RNAs RNA was purified from selected chromatographic peaks using TRIzol LS and following manufacturer's instructions. The obtained RNA was diluted in 8 μl of ultra-pure RNase-free water, and 7 μl were used as input for NGS library preparation using the NEBNext Small RNA Library Prep Set for Illumina (New England Biolabs).

description: Generate reporter protein constructs by replacing the RNA-binding RRM domains of TDP43 with GFP to create TDP43 RRM-GFP, which assembles into micron-sized liquid droplets suitable for quantitative dynamic analysis in live cells.
goal: to create a reporter system for rapid, quantitative analysis of CTD sequence variants in live cells
span_chunk: we replaced the RNA-binding RRM domains of TDP43 with GFP to generate a reporter protein (hereafter called TDP43 RRM-GFP) that assembles into micron-sized liquid droplets

description: Use automated confocal microscopy to monitor the nuclear and total GFP fluorescence in thousands of cells expressing TDP43 RRM-GFP with wild-type or mutant IDRs.
goal: to estimate changes in the critical concentration required for phase separation caused by IDR mutations
span_chunk: we combined high-throughput automated confocal microscopy and flow cytometry to monitor the nuclear and total GFP fluorescence in thousands of cells expressing TDP43 RRM-GFP with wild-type (WT) or mutant IDRs

description: Employ flow cytometry to analyze the nuclear and total GFP fluorescence in a large number of cells expressing TDP43 RRM-GFP, allowing for the estimation of the saturation concentration (C sat) for phase separation.
goal: to quantify the nuclear abundance of TDP43 RRM-GFP and its mutants in relation to phase separation propensity
span_chunk: we combined high-throughput automated confocal microscopy and flow cytometry to monitor the nuclear and total GFP fluorescence in thousands of cells expressing TDP43 RRM-GFP with wild-type (WT) or mutant IDRs

task_name: Assess phase separation using half-bleach FRAP experiments
description: Perform half-bleach fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (FRAP) experiments on TDP43 RRM-GFP droplets to evaluate their material properties and dynamics.
goal: to determine the influence of arginine-mediated interactions on the viscosity of TDP43 RRM-GFP condensates
span_chunk: Material properties of the large TDP43 RRM-GFP droplets can be readily assessed using half-bleach FRAP experiments

task_name: Analyze phase separation of full-length TDP43 in vitro
description: Purify full-length TDP43 with wild-type and variant CTDs from bacteria and investigate their phase separation behavior in vitro to validate the TDP43 RRM-GFP reporter assay findings.
goal: to corroborate the role of aromatic residues in phase separation of full-length TDP43
span_chunk: we purified full-length TDP43 with WT, F-S or FYW-S variant CTDs from bacteria and investigated their phase separation behavior in vitro

task_name: Test the effect of RNA on TDP43 phase separation
description: Evaluate the impact of RNA concentrations on the phase separation of purified WT and mutant TDP43 to understand the role of RNA in TDP43 condensate formation.
goal: to determine how RNA influences the phase separation of TDP43
span_chunk: Given that TDP43 is an RNA-binding protein, we next tested the effect of RNA on the phase separation of purified WT and mutant TDP43.

task_name: Perform live-cell imaging of TDP43 RRM-GFP
description: Use live-cell imaging to observe the formation and dynamics of TDP43 RRM-GFP condensates in cells, particularly focusing on mutants with altered numbers of hydrophobic clusters.
goal: to investigate the role of the number and spacing of hydrophobic clusters in TDP43 condensate dynamics
span_chunk: Live-cell imaging suggested that the 2 × Φ mutant immediately aggregates after translation, as we observed a much earlier onset of phase transition

task_name: Quantify exon skipping using flow cytometry
description: Employ a flow cytometry-compatible splicing reporter to measure the exon-skipping activity of TDP43 variants with single-cell resolution.
goal: to assess the splicing function of TDP43 variants in relation to their phase separation properties
span_chunk: To analyze the splicing activity of TDP43 variants rapidly, quantitatively and with single-cell resolution, we built a flow cytometry-compatible splicing reporter

description: Obtain a cell suspension from planaria and stain with Hoechst 33342 (nuclear dye) and MTG (mitochondrial dye).
goal: To label the nuclear content and mitochondrial mass of planarian cell populations for flow cytometry analysis.
span_chunk: The cell suspension of planaria was stained with Hoechst 33,342 (nuclear dye) and MTG.

description: Analyze the stained cell suspension using flow cytometry to identify distinct populations X1, X2, and Xins based on nuclear content and mitochondrial mass.
goal: To differentiate and quantify the planarian stem cell populations by their nuclear content and mitochondrial mass.
span_chunk: The cells stained with Hoechst showed three distinct populations, X1, X2, and Xins, based on their nuclear content.

description: Examine the MTG fluorescence in X1 and Xins cells to determine the distribution pattern in the cytoplasm.
goal: To observe the mitochondrial distribution differences between proliferating stem cells (X1) and differentiated cells (Xins).
span_chunk: MTG fluorescence in most X1 cells was more perinuclear and exhibited polarized distribution in the cytoplasm... Conversely, MTG fluorescence in Xins cells, in general, was evenly distributed in the cytoplasm.

description: Treat cells with Verapamil, an efflux pump inhibitor, and stain with MTG to test if the low MTG intensity in X1 and X2 cells is due to dye efflux.
goal: To confirm that the lower MTG fluorescence in X1 cells is an actual indicator of decreased mitochondrial mass and not due to dye efflux.
span_chunk: To test whether the low MTG intensity in X1 and X2 cells was a consequence of dye efflux, the cells were treated with Verapamil, an efflux pump inhibitor, and stained with MTG.

description: Clone the BCM1 gene from Arabidopsis to facilitate the expression and purification of the BCM1 protein.
goal: to obtain the BCM1 gene for subsequent expression in a suitable host system
span_chunk: To identify novel regulators of Chl biosynthesis and catabolism, we screened publicly available datasets for Arabidopsis genes of unknown function that exhibit the transcriptional signatures of CBGs or CCGs, and identified At2g35260, hereafter designated BCM1.
